name: VEML6040 RGBW colour sensor
description: Vishay RGBW colour sensor: 16-bit red, green, blue and white channels, ambient light in lux from the green channel (0.007865 lx/count up to 515 lx at 1280 ms, up to 16 496 lx at 40 ms) and colour temperature from R, G, B. I2C at the fixed address 0x10; the chip runs on 2.5-3.6 V. Sold as: VEML6040 RGBW colour sensor module (purple 4-pin clone board shared with the VEML6075, silkscreen 6075/6040, header VIN GND SCL SDA), with a 3.3 V regulator and I2C level shifting so it runs from 3.3-5 V.
eli5: Sees how much red, green, blue and white light falls on it, so your board can tell colours, brightness and how warm or cool a light is.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 3.3-5 V (regulated to 3.3 V on the board)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (pull-up and level shifter on board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (pull-up and level shifter on board)

supplierQuery: VEML6040 RGBW color sensor module I2C
buildNotes: Registers are 16-bit and travel LSB first: write [command, LSB, MSB]; read the command code with a repeated start (no stop) and get LSB then MSB.
CONF (0x00) low byte: IT in bits 6:4 (40/80/160/320/640/1280 ms), TRIG bit 2, AF bit 1, SD bit 0; high byte 0. Write SD = 0 to start measuring and wait one integration time before the first reading.
Results: R 0x08, G 0x09, B 0x0A, W 0x0B. Lux = G counts x sensitivity: 0.25168 lx/count at 40 ms, halving for each doubling of IT down to 0.007865 at 1280 ms.
Choose the integration time for the brightest light expected: 160 ms saturates (65535 counts) at about 4124 lx; use 40 ms outdoors.
Colour temperature (app note, empirical): CCT = 4278.6 x ((R - B) / G + 0.5)^-1.2455 K in open air; a cover glass changes the 0.5 offset.
The address is fixed at 0x10, the same as the VEML7700 and VEML6075: only one of them per I2C bus without a multiplexer.

The bright white LED on many of these modules shines into the sensor's surroundings; for ambient readings keep it from lighting the sensor, for colour-of-object readings hold the object a few mm away.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from veml6040 import VEML6040

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = VEML6040(i2c, it_ms=160)  # 0.06292 lx per G count, up to 4124 lx
while True:
    r, g, b, w = sensor.rgbw()
    cct = VEML6040.cct(r, g, b)
    print('Lux=%.2f R=%d G=%d B=%d W=%d CCT=%s' % (sensor.lux(g), r, g, b, w, '%.0fK' % cct if cct else '-'))
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Reports the light level, the four colour channels and the colour temperature set on the sliders
